The sun rises from the east.

The process of mitosis, which is cell division resulting in two identical daughter cells, involves several steps. It starts with prophase, where the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes and the nuclear membrane dissolves. During metaphase, chromosomes line up at the cell’s equator. Anaphase follows with sister chromatids being pulled apart to opposite poles of the cell. In telophase, chromosomes begin to decondense, and new nuclear membranes form around them. Finally, cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm, and two genetically identical daughter cells are produced.
